Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Acme Health is ready to move forward with a Dedicated GPU pool for inference (HIPAA adjacency; not storing PHI but strongly audited). High-level asks:

- Target steady-state throughput: 180 concurrent requests (~15k tokens/s) with p95 latency <200ms for our primary /generate route.
- Burst behavior: expect up to 3x traffic for short windows (5–20min) during peak business hours.
- Region preference: primary in us-west-2, failover in eu-west-1.
- Security: KMS-based key management, audit logging retention 13 months.
- Integrations: Private VPC peering + strict firewall rules (we'll provide network CIDRs).

Attached is a network diagram and our initial SOW draft. Would like to schedule a kickoff to align on provisioning checklist, autoscale/burst policy options, and handoff milestones. Availability next week is mostly Tue/Wed afternoons PST.

Thanks,

Claire / team — adding a draft checklist and policy options to prepare for kickoff. High-level items below; I'll attach a template for burst policy.

Staging checklist (pre-provision):
- Confirm VPC peering details + CIDR allowlist
- Provide KMS ARN and IAM principal for token encryption
- Desired retention for audit logs (default 13 months ok)
- Expected token-length percentiles (p50/p90/p95) and average request size
- SLA latency window and error budget tolerance

Sizing & burst policy options (pick one to start):
A) Conservative pool: baseline capacity for steady-state (180 conc) + 1.5x autoscale ceiling, 2-min cool-down.
B) Aggressive pool with short bursts: baseline + 3x burst slots allowed for 10–20 min windows; preemptible instances for burst capacity (lower cost).
C) Hybrid: baseline + staged burst where first tier is warm reserved, second tier is preemptible with graceful degradation to smaller model if capacity exhausted.

Questions for kickoff (please confirm):
- Which option aligns with procurement constraints? (preemptible usage needs approval)
- Maximum acceptable cold-start time for burst instances?
- Do you want automatic model fallback policy if capacity runs out?

Attachment: burst_policy_template.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)

I'll bring a recommended default (C) to the kickoff unless you prefer otherwise.

—Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

- Region: confirmed primary us-west-2; passive failover to eu-west-1 with DNS-based routing.
- Security: we will send KMS ARN and an additional SOC2 attestation request to Devindra for review.
